verdicts.evidence: For n=12, the max value of m such that there exist disjoint cross-intersecting families X, Y of size m is 1586 (using sets of size >= 7 and size >= 6). A more general bound or the specific problem from IMO SL 2004 confirms that for m=2004, n=13 is the minimum.

verdicts.label: B
verdicts.evidence: For n=13, we can take all subsets of size >= 7. There are 2^{12} = 4096 such subsets. Since any two subsets of size >= 7 in a set of 13 elements must intersect, any two disjoint collections X and Y chosen from these 4096 subsets will be cross-intersecting. Since 2*2004 = 4008 <= 4096, such an arrangement is possible. For n=12, the total number of subsets is 4096, and it can be shown that the size of the largest cross-intersecting disjoint families X, Y with |X|=|Y|=m is smaller than 2004.
